claims.statement: The server loads MCP connections in instance, workspace, then personal-owner order; a later source replaces any earlier connection with the same name, including a disabled or empty-allowlist override.

Personal MCP and Notion integrations are available only after private credential scope resolves: public threads yield no private credential login, and a private thread requires its saved owner to match the GitHub login that started the run.
MCP connection records are separated into instance, workspace-slug, and user-login Store namespaces, and legacy flat workspace_mcps records are adopted once into the instance tier.

Connection settings accept only HTTPS streamable HTTP or SSE endpoints and an explicit tool allowlist; URLs with credentials, fragments, or secret-like query parameters and unsafe or duplicate headers are rejected.

MCP headers and OAuth client secrets are encrypted at rest and excluded from public connection responses; saved credentials may be reused only from the prior record in the same scope, while changed destinations require replacement credentials.

Instance and workspace MCP dashboard APIs require an administrator, while personal APIs derive the connection scope from the signed-in session; header reveal returns no-store responses and validation errors are redacted.

MCP discovery initializes and paginates a remote catalog with duplicate-cursor and duplicate-name rejection, has a 30-second limit, and caches definitions by scope, connection name, and revision with ten-minute freshness and 24-hour maximum age.

Only allowlisted remote MCP definitions are exposed, and every wrapped call re-resolves its connection and refuses execution if the connection is disabled, changed, moved to another winning scope, or no longer allows that tool.

The MCP HTTP transport confines requests to the configured HTTPS origin, disables redirects and ambient proxy trust, resolves only public addresses, and pins a validated address while preserving the original Host and SNI.
Optional MCP loading fails closed: if source listing fails, no lower-precedence connection is exposed, and a catalog-discovery failure yields an empty tool list for that connection.

MCP OAuth supports only client credentials using client_secret_post or client_secret_basic, caches bearer tokens per owner namespace and credentials, refreshes before expiry, and retries a 401 once with a fresh token.

Notion OAuth discovers and dynamically registers against HTTPS mcp.notion.com endpoints, uses PKCE S256, and stores temporary code-verifier and client-secret material encrypted until the flow is consumed.

Notion user credentials are encrypted under user_credentials/<login>, are fail-soft when used to gate optional tools, refresh under a per-login lock, and delete a stored connection when refresh requires reauthorization.

Notion tools use the hosted streamable HTTP MCP server with a bearer token, and their wrappers obtain a fresh token and tool at invocation time after confirming the private credential owner, so catalog loading does not grant durable access.

LangSmith Gateway routing is optional and centralized in make_model: workspace settings override the deployment default, supported providers receive gateway base URL and LangSmith credentials, and unsupported providers or missing keys fall back to direct calls.

Focused tests cover MCP scope isolation and catalog behavior, transport containment, OAuth token lifecycle and redaction, dashboard credential boundaries, and Notion OAuth and call-time token refresh.
